items.title: CVE-2026-60004: Critical Gitea RCE (CVSS 9.8) Actively Exploited, Dropping Miner Payloads — CISA KEV
items.summary: A critical remote code execution flaw in Gitea (CVSS 9.8) allows any user with repository write access to execute arbitrary shell commands as the Gitea OS user via a git hook injection in the diffpatch API. On open-registration instances, an attacker can register a free account and immediately exploit the chain. CISA added it to the KEV catalog with a federal remediation deadline already passed. Attackers are deploying cryptocurrency miner-like payloads and establishing persistence.
items.why: Gitea is broadly self-hosted in enterprise DevSecOps pipelines. The near-zero exploitation bar — any authenticated user on default open-registration instances — combined with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation makes this critical. Patch to 1.27.1 immediately and disable open registration.

items.title: CISA KEV: Critical macOS, SharePoint, VMware vCenter & Microsoft IKE Flaws Confirmed Actively Exploited
items.summary: CISA added four critical vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog in a single update: CVE-2026-65400 (Apple macOS), CVE-2026-55040 (Microsoft SharePoint), CVE-2026-59310 (Broadcom VMware vCenter), and CVE-2026-33824 (Microsoft IKE Service Extensions). All four are confirmed exploited in the wild. The vCenter flaw is of particular concern given its prevalence in enterprise virtualization environments.
items.why: Four distinct CVEs spanning Apple, Microsoft, and Broadcom ecosystems in one KEV update signals a broad active exploitation wave. The vCenter flaw is especially dangerous — hypervisor compromise gives attackers control over all virtual machines and is a hallmark of ransomware pre-positioning. Patch or isolate affected systems immediately.
items.source: The Hacker News / CISA KEV Catalog

items.title: Salt Typhoon (China-Nexus APT) Has Compromised Networks in 80+ Countries Across Telecoms, Transport & Government
items.summary: CrowdStrike's 2026 Global Threat Report reveals that the Chinese APT Salt Typhoon has compromised networks across more than 80 countries spanning telecommunications, transportation, and government sectors. The campaign represents one of the broadest cyber-espionage operations ever documented, with the group likely maintaining persistent wiretap-level access to significant portions of global communications infrastructure.
items.why: The geographic scope (80+ countries) combined with Salt Typhoon's focus on telco backbones means this group likely has access to a major portion of global voice and data communications. The CrowdStrike report also notes average eCrime breakout time is now just 29 minutes and adversary AI-enabled attack volume rose 89% year over year.

items.title: Iranian APT 'Screening Serpens' Escalates Post-Conflict Espionage with Dual RAT Families Across Five Countries
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 tracked Screening Serpens, an Iran-nexus APT that significantly escalated operations following the regional conflict that began in February 2026. The group has deployed two distinct new RAT variant families against entities across at least five countries, focusing on credential harvesting and intelligence collection. The campaign demonstrates how geopolitical events directly accelerate nation-state cyber operations.
items.why: Purpose-built dual-RAT deployment suggests coordinated, parallel intelligence-gathering campaigns across multiple sectors simultaneously. Organizations in the Middle East, Europe, and allied nations in energy, defense, and government should elevate vigilance, review spear-phishing exposure, and rotate credentials.

items.title: Mandiant M-Trends 2026: Attackers Hand Off Access in 22 Seconds; 28% of CVEs Exploited Within 24h of Disclosure
items.summary: Mandiant's M-Trends 2026 report — based on 500,000+ hours of frontline incident response — finds that threat actors are handing off compromised access to follow-on operators in as little as 22 seconds, reflecting fully automated initial-access pipelines. Additionally, 28.3% of all CVEs are now exploited within 24 hours of public disclosure, and identity was the primary attack vector in nearly 90% of all investigations. Ransomware accounted for 13% of investigations, targeting backup and virtualization infrastructure to deny recovery.
items.why: The 22-second handoff metric means defenders have almost no window to detect and respond after initial access. The 28.3% same-day exploitation rate makes the traditional patch window effectively zero for critical vulnerabilities. Organizations must shift to runtime controls, assume-breach postures, and identity-centric defenses rather than relying on patching timelines.
